author: illustration
headline: Felixstowe congested and London Gateway wind stoppage likely Saturday
standfirst: Action needed at Felixstowe (congested), London Gateway (disruption likely), Liverpool (watch), Rotterdam (watch). Inbound: weather may delay transatlantic and Cape-routed Asia arrivals into the Channel by up to 1 day. Reliability: Sea-Intelligence 49.9%, Xeneta 29%.

watchlist_notes.western_approaches: Watch risk of heavy weather Thu 1 Oct (sea 4.86 m, wind 10.2 m/s). Trend: improving.

port_notes.felixstowe: Berth occupancy 84%, 13 pp above normal. Add 2–3 days to inland plans for containers arriving in the next 2 weeks, pre-book haulage and check your free time.
port_notes.southampton: Running as expected with no predicted delays. Speak to your carrier about release and delivery now to keep it that way.
port_notes.london_gateway: Crane stoppages likely Sat 3 Oct 11:00–20:00 with gusts to 22 m/s. Tell your haulier to expect longer waits and allow 24–48 hours on collections.
port_notes.liverpool: Intermittent crane stoppages possible Sun 4 Oct 07:00–13:00. Allow 12–24 hours and avoid tight Sunday cut-offs.
port_notes.rotterdam: Busier than usual at 7 pp above normal occupancy. Keep an eye on berthing times if you tranship here and avoid tight feeder connections.
port_notes.antwerp: Running as expected with no predicted delays. Speak to your carrier about release and delivery now.
port_notes.bremerhaven: Ships spending 36% longer in port than usual. Add 2–3 days to inland plans for containers arriving in the next 2 weeks and pre-book haulage.
port_notes.hamburg: Reported 24-hour strike on Monday. Check your terminal's latest notice before booking collections and allow 24–48 hours.

inbound_note: Western Approaches: Expect transatlantic and Cape-routed Asia arrivals into the Channel to run up to 1 day late.
